title: Anthropic IPO Investors Struggle to Put a Price on Rogue AI Risk
key_facts: Bloomberg reports that investors considering Anthropic's planned IPO are struggling to value a company that some fear could help wipe out humanity.

A debate began when researchers posted on X about a 10% or greater chance that AI would wipe out humanity; Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei weighed in with an essay on losing control of AI systems, cyberattacks, bioterrorism and economic disruption.

Venture capitalist Sam Lessin of Slow Ventures proposed that AI labs be forced to put $1 trillion in escrow for possible cleanup, and said liabilities might be a $2 trillion or $4 trillion risk to society.
Anthropic plans to raise as much or more in its IPO as SpaceX, whose $86.2 billion IPO in June has traded more than 20% above its offer price; Anthropic's valuation could reach $2 trillion.
Insurers say coverage for AI businesses is hard to find; analyst Kevin Moss said the safety debate was unlikely to upset the IPO plans.
Joe Ziolkowski of Relm Insurance said investors are unlikely to discount IPO prices for exposures they cannot quantify.
An Anthropic spokesperson declined to comment.
quote_evidence: Investors considering Anthropic PBC's planned mega-IPO are grappling with an unusual conundrum: How to value a company that some fear could help wipe out the human race.
A spokesperson for Anthropic declined to comment.
why_it_matters_hint: It shows that AI safety risk, hard to measure, is becoming a question for investors as well as regulators.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked; Bloomberg text read on Moneycontrol. Several views are opinions quoted by Bloomberg (Lessin, Moss, Ziolkowski), not findings.
